topIssues.title: fix(auth): serialize Steward session authority across browser tabs
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
<!-- goal-29918-current-summary-30249 -->
## Current integration status — 2026-09-06

**Open; not yet accepted.** Existing #30257 is already Ready, with conflicts and CHANGES_REQUESTED. The claimed 37-file local integration is unpushed; scoped checks pass but independent reviews still request corrections; final validation/review and real two-context staging proof remain.

[Current candidate, evidence and next action](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/30249#issuecomment-5559619997) · [active bounded claim](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/30249#issuecomment-5559693298). No replacement PR or issue is needed.
<!-- /goal-29918-current-summary -->

Parent: #29918, under #25020

Related auth/session owner lanes: #20848 and #29889.

## Problem

Steward browser authority is serialized only inside one JavaScript realm. The SSO bridge queue, logout epoch, cookie-sync abort controller, passive `AuthTokenSync` dedupe, shared token mutation queue, refresh single-flight, and several callback/restore paths are module-local. Two same-origin tabs can therefore mutate the browser token and HttpOnly session cookie out of order.

Concrete failure classes reproduced from current source inspection:

- tab A can finish a stale token-to-cookie POST after tab B logs out;
- two accounts can leave localStorage bound to token B while the final HttpOnly cookie was set by token A;
- logout followed by a fresh login can let an older operation resume unless logout authority uses a non-resettable generation (ABA);
- a stale passive sync or refresh response can clear or republish authority owned by a newer tab.

This is pre-existing on `develop@63368527be1221e2b45236d308c87d5bc2f50b7d` and is not introduced by #30243. That PR explicitly limits its guarantee to the same browser realm; a bridge-local lock would be incomplete because cookie/token mutations also occur in login callbacks, refresh, startup restore, repair, first-run, native apps studio, and passive session mirroring.

## Acceptance criteria

- Use one origin-wide coordinator for every browser operation whose request/response can mutate Steward cookies or canonical token authority: session sync, nonce exchange, refresh, callback/restore writes, passive mirroring, logout, and cookie DELETE cleanup.
- Use a durable opaque logout generation stored separately from the UX auto-bridge marker. Advance it on every logout and never clear/reset it, so logout → fresh login → stale completion cannot pass an ABA check.
- Capture expected token/generation before work and revalidate inside the coordinator before persistence, before cookie mutation, after response settlement, and before publishing/clearing markers.
- Bound every network operation held by the coordinator with timeout/abort; a crashed or hung tab must not strand login/logout for the origin.
- Treat `session_ended` and `invalid_token` as definitive only at the documented server boundary, and clear only the exact authority that received the rejection.
- If origin-wide coordination is unavailable, automatic SSO must fail closed to ordinary login rather than claim a safe cross-tab bridge.
- Add deterministic two-context coverage for logout during persistence, logout during cookie sync, inverse A/B responses, ABA logout/login/resume, stale passive sync, refresh/logout overlap, and cleanup DELETE ordering.
- Pin live staging acceptance to an exact deployed SHA with two real same-origin contexts; mocked storage events alone are insufficient.

## Coordination note

This issue owns only the cross-tab session-authority primitive and its integration boundaries. It should coordinate with @lalalune / @wakesync on #20848 and the hosted logout owner on #29889 rather than duplicating their one-document or server-logout acceptance work. No deployment, provider action, identity mutation, or production change is requested here.

topIssues.title: Diagnose and eliminate delayed trailing speech in product voice playback
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem and scope
The user reports the final word or section arriving separately after the rest of a spoken response. Source inspection identifies a relevant segmentation/playback boundary, but this research has not reproduced the audible defect or measured its root cause.

[packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts:2670](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/06963a19b01c3720aedcf77c77434936e8654270/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2670) queues unsent prefixes and final remainders; playback is serialized. [packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-types.ts:388](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/06963a19b01c3720aedcf77c77434936e8654270/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-types.ts#L388) configures first/later chunk thresholds and debounce. The local [plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/phrase-chunker.ts:47](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/06963a19b01c3720aedcf77c77434936e8654270/plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/phrase-chunker.ts#L47) already supports timer and final flushes. Investigate the active product path before changing these policies.

## Acceptance
- Reproduce the reported symptom on the actual configured provider and capture final text arrival, synthesis dispatch/first PCM, previous clip end, next clip start, and final playback completion.
- Preserve every speakable token exactly once and in order across a one-word tail, punctuation-free ending, slow token arrival, multiple clauses, Unicode/numbers, stream-to-final message promotion, interruption, and the next turn.
- Fix the measured cause and demonstrate before/after gap measurements plus human-listened natural speech; do not trade reduced delay for clipped words or degraded prosody.
- Verify browser/cloud and desktop/local paths separately where affected; explicitly identify any untested path.

## Existing work and evidence
Coordinate with Nubs's draft [#29492](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/29492), which owns duplex/handoff/crossfade and still requires real audible acceptance. Reuse tracing under [#28214](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/28214); distinguish PSTN lifecycle failures in [#26722](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/26722). Use the canonical VoiceScenario/workbench rather than a new harness. Inspect real audio, provider/transport logs, and complete model trajectories in a verified evidence bundle, tied to installed/deployed SHA. Run owning-package checks, root verify, and applicable app audit. A mock-only green is not acoustic proof.

Estimate: 2–4 person-days; Nubs. Linked files were clean at the inspected HEAD; other shared-working-tree edits were preserved.

## Critical source audit and implementation plan — 2026-09-06

Audited develop snapshot: `8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048`. This is a source/caller/test review, not a reproduced acoustic failure or a completion claim. No dependency installation, provider request, microphone capture, or audio playback was performed. Issue body/comments and draft #29492 were read live; the latter is OPEN and draft at `b209c79fe2ac1bde176204f078834f9352b8395c`, with genuine audible overlap acceptance still pending.

### What already exists and what is actually missing

- **There are distinct active product paths.** [useShellVoiceOutput, lines 107–151](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/components/shell/useShellVoiceOutput.ts#L107) explicitly disables the message-to-TTS watcher when Cartesia realtime is enabled because Sonic already streams audio. The old issue's `useVoiceChat` links are relevant to non-realtime output and explicit playback, but are not evidence that this code causes a realtime Talk symptom. Record the real mode, endpoint, selected provider/model/voice, device, and installed SHA before implementing a fix.
- **Legacy output does queue a final remainder.** [queueAssistantSpeech, lines 2805–2876](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2805) tracks the submitted prefix, promotes temporary message IDs, flushes final text, and debounces incomplete text. The [24/88 character thresholds and 170 ms debounce](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-types.ts#L387) are present, not missing functionality.
- **Source-confirmed latency mechanism, acoustic attribution unverified:** [the queue worker](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2381) serially awaits each provider's speak operation. For local and ElevenLabs paths, fetching the entire response, decoding, and playback completion are inside that operation ([ElevenLabs lines 1767–1774](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L1767), [local lines 2101–2107](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2101)). A queued next clip therefore starts its synthesis after prior playback finishes; the resulting gap includes network/synthesis/decode latency. Whether that is the reported final-word symptom needs timestamps and listening.
- **Segmentation risks to reproduce:** threshold and debounce flushes can submit the current text without a complete word or sentence boundary. A subsequently arriving suffix can become a separate TTS utterance. The [remainder helper](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-playback.ts#L196) accepts case-insensitive/interior matches and returns an empty string when a submitted prefix is no longer found. Audit final text reconciliation and Unicode normalization explicitly; do not assume arbitrary final rewrites are lossless prefix extensions.
- **Existing local support must be reused:** [scheduler final flushing](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/scheduler.ts#L287) and [timer-driven flushing](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/scheduler.ts#L894) already exist. Adding another chunker or reducing a timeout globally is not justified without path evidence.
- Existing behavioral tests cover temporary-ID promotion and remainder deduplication in `useVoiceChat.bidirectional.test.tsx:198–245`, and streaming/final promotion in `useVoiceChat.tts-playback.test.tsx:415`. Those use controlled playback, not real acoustic acceptance. The playback implementation checks cancellation generation before and after decode (`voice-chat-audio-playback.ts:65–67`); preserve those guards.

### Ordered implementation work

1. **Nubs / product voice owner: establish the failing trace.** Extend canonical VoiceScenario/workbench coverage with the exact reported reply, a one-word tail, punctuation-free reply, slow tokens, and a final frame whose text is identical to the last stream frame. Tie text-arrival and audio events to session/turn/message/segment IDs; record final text arrival, phrase submission, provider dispatch, first received PCM, actual previous playback end, actual next playback start, EOS and final drain. Keep payload-free operational timing logs and separately controlled complete trajectories for evidence.
2. **UI + realtime owner: classify the dominant delay.** For non-realtime output, distinguish text accumulation delay from serial synthesis and decode delay. For realtime Talk, trace `voice-session-client.ts`, `voice-session-playback.ts` and server EOS/phrase continuation through the actual Sonic path; do not change the disabled watcher as the sole fix. Native mobile branches through TalkMode (`useVoiceChat.ts:2410`) and requires its own timing boundary rather than treating JS dispatch as first audible PCM.
3. **Implement only the measured fix.** If serial synthesis dominates, prepare the next complete segment while current audio plays and commit prepared audio in original order, with bounded concurrent work/backpressure that never drops text. If word fragmentation dominates, retain the incomplete lexical tail and flush it losslessly on final/EOS; preserve ordered offsets and explicit reconciliation for non-prefix final text. If EOS/drain dominates, correct that lifecycle directly. Any lookahead/batching policy must preserve first-audio responsiveness and natural prosody; do not switch every response to final-only playback as an unmeasured workaround.
4. **Make cancellation and completion structural.** Carry immutable turn/generation/segment ownership through preparation, fetch, decode, scheduling and drain. Interruption cancels the old generation; stale completion cannot enqueue into the next turn. Mark final playback completion only after the last audio frame drains. Handle synthesis failures as visible typed boundary errors, not silence reported as success.
5. **Coordinate overlapping work before editing.** #29492 owns realtime duplex/handoff/crossfade; reconcile exact current head/path overlap and retain its audible acceptance gate. #30680 owns short phrase eligibility and cache identity, while #30356 owns provider dispatch/settlement and duplicate warm requests. Share timing and call-count instrumentation. #28214 remains the tracing/evidence dependency and #26722 owns PSTN lifecycle differences.

### Verification and acceptance receipts

- Add consumer-boundary regressions with a controllable token stream and real queue logic: partial final word, one-word final segment, whitespace/Unicode/decimal/abbreviation boundaries, multiple clauses, rewritten final text, temporary-ID promotion, identical final frame, cancellation during preparation/decode/playback, next turn, provider error, and queued backpressure. Assert complete speakable content exactly once in order, request counts, stale-audio exclusion and final-drain timing. Helper-only threshold tests are insufficient.
- Run affected UI and local-inference focused suites through their package Vitest harnesses, then owning package tests/typecheck/read-only lint, shared/cloud gates if touched, root `bun run verify`, and `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app` for affected shared UI. Missing dependencies in this research checkout are not test failures; no suite pass is claimed here.
- Capture before/after real provider audio and human listening on browser/cloud and desktop/local independently, with exact installed/deployed SHA, provider settings, raw timing receipt and p50/p95 boundary gaps over repeated cold/warm runs. Agree the acceptable gap/prosody budget from baseline before tuning; do not fabricate a universal threshold. Include complete untruncated text/trajectory, audio, applicable desktop/mobile captures, console/network/backend logs, and MP4 in the canonical verified evidence bundle. Mobile paths require real supported-device proof if modified; otherwise explicitly identify them as untested.
- Close only after the reproduced trailing delay is eliminated without omitted, repeated or clipped words and with clean interruption and subsequent-turn playback. Existing source features and draft PR checks alone cannot satisfy this.

Planning: retain 2–4 person-days as a provisional research range; re-estimate after step 1 identifies whether one path or both realtime and buffered playback require changes. No implementation ownership claim or board-status change is made by this audit.

## Independent deep review: #30679

Audited `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`. Three concrete counterexamples refine the original buffering plan; no audio/device run was performed.

### P1 — A corrected final frame can be silently discarded while marked final (reproduced)

Executed `/tmp/guardian-project19-deep-review/probe-30679.ts` with Bun. It extracts the unchanged production `queueAssistantSpeech` callback and real text-boundary/remainder helpers; collaborators capture tasks instead of playing audio. For the same message ID:

1. Streaming frame `The available option is red.` queues that sentence.
2. Final frame `Actually, the available option is blue.` queues **nothing**.
3. State records `latestSpeakable` as the corrected final, `queuedSpeakablePrefix` as the stale red sentence, and `finalQueued:true`.

[remainderAfter](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-playback.ts#L185-L207) returns empty when prior text is not a prefix/interior substring; the [consumer](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2816-L2829) treats that as no remaining speech and marks completion. The original plan must specify a non-monotonic stream contract, not only buffer sizes. Do not blindly replay the full final (duplicates already spoken words); distinguish queued-but-unplayed text, actual played content, and replacement/correction events. Reject unsupported rewrites explicitly or deliver a deliberate corrected utterance with clear ownership.

Second actual probe: `Hello there.` → final `Note: Hello there. More.` queues only `Hello there.` and `More.`. Interior-substring recovery drops `Note:` but records the whole final as queued. Remove silent interior matching; acceptance must compare the actual delivered text sequence against the authorized append/revision contract.

These are deterministic boundary counterexamples, not proof that every production provider rewrites text. Current shell [provisional-frame suppression](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/components/shell/useShellVoiceOutput.ts#L175-L186) specifically protects one known wholesale-replacement path and must remain. Other callers, direct hook use, and non-provisional replacement still require a defined contract.

### P2 — Monotonic text alone does not make chunk boundaries pronounceable (reproduced)

Actual callback probe: partial `I am checking the international` followed by final `I am checking the internationalization settings.` queues two independent requests: `I am checking the international` and `ization settings.`. The [threshold branch](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2831-L2842) sends the entire partial string once it exceeds 24 characters, even when the final word may still be streaming. The debounce flush has the same unresolved trailing-word problem at lines 2669–2706. This is an exact request segmentation defect; no specific acoustic measurement is claimed.

Amend prefetch work to retain an unfinished lexical suffix until a stable delimiter or final event, with language-aware handling where spaces are not word boundaries. A timer does not prove word completion. Preserve all characters and ordering; do not use a maximum-length truncation to repair prosody. Test token streams split inside words, Unicode graphemes, decimal numbers, abbreviations and URLs, then inspect real spoken continuity on supported targets.

### P2 — Latency improvement must separate synthesis scheduling from playback completion

The [worker](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2382-L2532) awaits each provider's full speak operation. [Decoded playback](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-audio-playback.ts#L130-L168) resolves on completion/timeout. Thus a later clip is synthesized only after earlier playback finishes on the buffered local/ElevenLabs path; faster segmentation alone cannot hide that synthesis interval. Implement bounded prefetch with one ordered playback owner and cancelable generation. Bound retained audio bytes/concurrency, not text completeness.

### Examined protections, ownership and acceptance amendments

Decoded playback checks generation both before and after asynchronous decode (`voice-chat-audio-playback.ts` lines 65–67); do not allege a missing decode cancellation guard. `cancelPlayback` increments generation, clears queue, aborts active fetch, and completes the playback waiter; retain all four when prefetch adds multiple requests. Reject late prefetched audio for old generations and test cancellation during synthesis, decode, and playback. Provider failure already fails closed. Coordinate the queue configuration/key race with #30680 so prefetch cannot synthesize one voice and label/cache another.

The shell message watcher explicitly exits for Cartesia realtime (`useShellVoiceOutput.ts` lines 147–151). This report's buffered-path findings must not be presented as a diagnosis of realtime Sonic. Live GitHub inspection confirms #29492 remains OPEN/DRAFT at `b209c79fe2ac1bde176204f078834f9352b8395c`; reusing its work requires exact-head review, not assuming it is merged. HEAD's #30723 changes native HTTP stream metadata validation; it does not repair these queue/text boundaries.

Require evidence for the exact target/provider reproducing the user's symptom: full authorized text vs queued/synthesized/played intervals, first-audio time, inter-clip silence, final-frame arrival, cancellation outcome, and subjective playback review. Pure task-capture probes above establish text loss/splitting but cannot establish acoustic latency or native playback success.

### Independent long-reply finding and repair in progress

The human listening acceptance above applies to the exact short recordings. A separate live navigation test exposed a longer reply ending mid-sentence: 180 words of generated text produced 22.6 seconds of Kokoro audio, and independent ASR found only 87 spoken words. The standalone scheduler passed the entire reply as one phrase; the native Kokoro tokenizer silently retained only its first 510 phoneme tokens.

The repair preflights every segment of the complete utterance before synthesis, splits at word boundaries while preserving ordered text, rejects an indivisible oversized word before emitting a prefix, and sends the same checked IPA to the native ABI v14+ IPA entry. Old libraries without that entry and exhausted audio allocations return explicit errors. Cancellation prevents later segment dispatch.

The exact captured reply now produces 43.875 seconds of real Kokoro audio (SHA-256 `4f335c87ec0087d0c33a79f92df4c94ff26d6c2e279a6ba42bb5eb080f2806ab`). Independent native CPU Qwen3-ASR 0.6B transcription covered every feature section and the exact final sentence, “Tell me what you want to write down first.” Minor ASR wording and punctuation differences remain. The full inference suite passed 2,916 tests across 282 files plus 60 native harness tests; 19 tests were explicitly skipped. Typecheck and lint passed. Independent review then found a separator-only suffix could produce empty IPA after a valid prefix; follow-up `9564979b97` rejects it during complete preflight, with 29 focused tests passing. Follow-up independent review found no remaining actionable defect and independently passed all 29 boundary tests plus the installed-phonemizer adversarial probe. Final root validation remains pending. This is recorded-audio proof, not microphone or all-provider acceptance.

The shell failure/retry recording, desktop/mobile captures, exact human-reviewed clips, and actual application audio are [attached inline](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/30679#issuecomment-5557739959). The native macOS file picker resolved the browser upload failure without changing extension permissions. The MP4 uses explanatory narration; actual application speech is attached separately.


The complete repaired long reply is available as [the original 43.875-second WAV](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31876611/long-reply-complete.wav), SHA-256 `4f335c87ec0087d0c33a79f92df4c94ff26d6c2e279a6ba42bb5eb080f2806ab`. Its independent ASR reaches the final sentence quoted above; the requesting user's earlier listening approval applies only to the two short clips. The implementation is now rebased without changes to the affected UI/native-inference source onto `cd821540d7`; current branch head `9743eb1a4cb94a0f3d14020675e4365f5121c2b0`.

Advances #23093, #23094 and #23095; also supplies the consent-bound registration prerequisite for #30638. These issues remain open. Pending hosted and live-integration acceptance.

# Behavior

Stripe terminal observations now publish lifecycle history, receipt, entitlement projection, policy generation and cancellation notice intent atomically. A failed write rolls back the whole transition. Historical event replay cannot restore older subscription authority.

Session-authorized managers can schedule and undo period-end cancellation. Commands record dispatch provenance before mutation and verify canonical Customer/subscription state before publication. Uncertain outcomes reconcile by retrieval without an automatic second mutation. Undo requires the captured schedule lineage to remain valid before dispatch. Tenant-scoped pending-command pagination exposes stale source identity and command uncertainty. Scheduling cancellation preserves current access until an effective terminal transition.

Existing-v1 paid renewal verifies the complete invoice, subscription, Customer, PaymentIntent, captured charge and catalog binding before granting allowance. Only a full captured, non-refunded, unadjusted monthly payment for an adjacent effective period can publish. Duplicate invoice/event delivery cannot grant twice. Unsupported observations retain retryable incident state.

Resource and inference admission use the same primary policy generation as billing snapshots. Cached paid state refreshes after a committed Free transition; missing or ambiguous required canonical authority is unavailable. Canonical-none non-subscriber accounts retain their existing legacy fallback. New allowance reservations and snapshot spendability share current organization/source/projection/period/grant identity checks. Denied spending is explicitly unavailable while ledger amounts remain intact; eligible exhausted allowance reports an observed zero. Historical reservations retain their settlement/refund ownership.

Generic app billing registration records owner and infrastructure-payer provenance and creates individual buyer accounts only after existing app consent. Merchant and subscription policy remain explicitly unconfigured. Cancellation notices have immutable identity, one durable attempt and distinct accepted/rejected/uncertain/unavailable outcomes. Dispatch requires server-approved per-revision recipients, content and delivery window. Missing policy does not send; uncertain SMTP acceptance does not trigger automatic resend or prove delivery.

The existing authenticated Stripe cron also recovers missed terminal observations using read-only canonical SDK requests. Durable leases, retry scheduling and complete-body deadlines bound provider work without retrying writes. Recovery publishes source/projection/generation/notice atomically and preserves webhook watermark provenance. Matching later events use a no-op only for a durably applied recovery revision with a coherent projection; ordinary webhook behavior is unchanged. Independent cron lanes retain failures and successful receipts separately.

Current head `2d85438b7c8cd54a38227dd3376e10033a07e5d6`, rebased on `c2d55bf5e460055c19fb0c8bdfe217e4f1b2c8d8` (41 commits).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Own the login SDK and identity service as `@elizaos/login`. Replace external Steward package/source dependencies across desktop, Cloud and application consumers. Export React login components and wallet providers from the `@elizaos/ui` root barrel, with lazy wallet adapters and no `/login` package subpath. Remove unused trading/DeFi routes and SDK methods, the unreferenced trade-order/provider-action evaluators, their spend tracker and venue catalog; retain authentication, linking, MFA, recovery and required wallet contracts. Fix durable initialization, grant isolation, Node package resolution and graceful service shutdown. React logout now waits for access/refresh revocation and reports retryable failures; refresh revocation uses its verified tenant context. Correct IPv6 loopback parsing for HSTS. Configure a filtered Railpack deployment and resolve the shared error class from portable source in Cloudflare. Verify the standard migration ledger before startup, scope wallet provisioning and login audit writes to their tenant, and use one session verifier backed by the existing bootstrap authority query.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature and dependency migration with authentication correctness fixes.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): preserve state and resource authority across lifecycle retries
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
This change preserves recoverable agent state and exact provider ownership across payment suspension, funded resume, replacement and deletion retries. A failed provider acknowledgement stays retryable. Cleanup uses the captured container, physical host and lifecycle generation, and cannot release a replacement host’s capacity or cancel deletion after teardown admission. Restored apps retain their configuration and credentials atomically, with outbound automation disabled.

The additional cleanup work retains a durable resource manifest covering compute, volumes, VPN and secrets. Ordinary replacement attempts now retain their placement and capacity authority before remote effects. A terminal or retried image job admits abandoned provider-success candidates into cleanup before releasing its execution binding. The existing daemon reconciles those records without treating lease expiry or missing acknowledgement as proof of absence. Recoverable volumes remain retained pending verified state recovery; compute absence alone does not authorize disk reclamation.

The exact restore provider additionally forces a quarantine marker into the container environment. In newly built images, the canonical shell entrypoint exits before normal startup when marked. A Linux/Docker counterfactual proved that the old script dispatched and wrote fixture state while the new one refused and left the candidate untouched. Historical images may lack this guard; image compatibility admission is still required. The provider-to-shell test and owning entrypoint tests passed.

The agent component work materializes a staged PGlite backup into an isolated candidate through the existing protected filesystem boundary. It checks the complete compressed digest, record order, archive paths and entry types; installs private files and directories; and persists/readbacks a replay-bound finish receipt. This does not open the production runtime, seal the cloud candidate, publish routing, or produce an activation MAC.

Tracks #23098, #22916, #20726 and #30746. This branch includes the earlier lifecycle work associated with the now-closed, unmerged prerequisite PRs #30714, #30745 and #30790. A range-diff against the previous published head e403b1b260be0351b3910d7a6ff49a3da68a1325 confirms all 40 earlier patches are unchanged after rebasing; nine commits extend that work.
